'''Revised A New Hope''' is the white-border Revised Unlimited reprint of [[A New Hope Limited]], published by Decipher in September 1998 as the 15th Star Wars CCG product.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]; online edition: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022023930/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/collecting.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher.com (Wayback, 4 May 1999)</ref><ref>[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/A_New_Hope_Limited A New Hope Limited] at Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260609070431/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/A_New_Hope_Limited Internet Archive]</ref>

It reprints the 162-card Limited pool. Most cards use Special Edition–era revised text. For example, "Adds 2 to the power of anything he pilots" replaces "Adds 2 to the power of any starship he pilots". The card list is below.

== Packaging ==
Sold in 9-card booster packs (MSRP $2.50: 5 commons, 3 uncommons, 1 rare) and 30-pack boxes. Each box included a fold-out Rules Supplement.<ref name="encyc" />

| [[File:ANH-L-undercover.gif|200px|link=Undercover (Revised)]] || [[Undercover (Revised)]] || [[Effect|Effect]] || U2 || 5 || Deploy on your spy at a site and cross spy to opponent’s side. Spy is now Undercover. During your deploy phase, may voluntarily “break cover” (lose Effect) if at a site. (Immune to Alter.) A special characteristic of spies activated by the Effect card Undercover (and certain other cards). Your Undercover spy operates with unique capabilities. It has no presence, but prevents your opponent from Force draining where present and allows deployment of your cards to the same location. (Even Undercover droid spies provide this benefit.) An Undercover spy does not participate in battles and may not be targeted by an opponent’s weapons in battle. To indicate that your spy is Undercover, place it on your opponent’s side of the table at the same site. Your Undercover spy moves during your opponent’s move phase (under your control and at normal use of your Force). An Undercover spy can board an opponent’s starship or vehicle (embark, shuttle, transfer etc.) if there is sufficient capacity; however, the opponent has the first chance to fill that capacity. If your Undercover spy is a pilot, it can operate an opponent’s unpiloted starship. Your Undercover spy may not board your own vehicle or starship card (although it may go to a vehicle or starship site). Despite being on the opponent’s side of a location and moving like one of your opponent’s characters, your Undercover spy is still your character, and is affected as one of your characters.
|-

(Revised)]] || [[Effect|Effect]] || U2 || 3 || Use 3 Force to deploy on table and stack one just-played interrupt here. To play any new Interrupt of the same name, player must first stack it here and use +1 Force for each Interrupt in stack, even if Interrupt is normally free. (Immune to Control.)
